import pandas as pd
from datetime import timedelta

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Extract high_ts from watermark (single row)
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    
    # Filter events: event_ts > high_ts
    new_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # Sort events by user_id, event_ts, event_seq for sequential processing
    new_events = new_events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Initialize result as a dict keyed by user_id for efficient updates
    snapshot_dict = {}
    for _, row in target_snapshot.iterrows():
        user_id = row["user_id"]
        snapshot_dict[user_id] = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "email": row["email"],
            "status": row["status"],
            "status_ts": row["status_ts"]
        }
    
    # Process each event sequentially
    for _, event in new_events.iterrows():
        user_id = event["user_id"]
        event_ts = event["event_ts"]
        op = event["op"]
        email = event["email"]
        
        # Get current state or initialize as new user
        if user_id not in snapshot_dict:
            current = {
                "user_id": user_id,
                "email": None,
                "status": None,
                "status_ts": None
            }
        else:
            current = snapshot_dict[user_id]
        
        if op == "D":
            # Soft delete: preserve email, set status to DELETED
            current["status"] = "DELETED"
            current["status_ts"] = event_ts
            # Email is preserved from before; if new user, set it
            if current["email"] is None or pd.isna(current["email"]):
                current["email"] = email
            # Note: email stays as-is on deletion
            
        elif op == "U":
            current_status = current["status"]
            current_status_ts = current["status_ts"]
            
            if current_status is None or pd.isna(current_status) or current_status == "ACTIVE":
                # New user or ACTIVE user: perform upsert
                current["email"] = email
                current["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                current["status_ts"] = event_ts
            elif current_status == "DELETED":
                # Deleted user: check resurrection window
                # Resurrection allowed if event_ts > status_ts + 7 days (strict inequality)
                seven_days = timedelta(days=7)
                if event_ts > current_status_ts + seven_days:
                    # Resurrect: update email and status
                    current["email"] = email
                    current["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                    current["status_ts"] = event_ts
                # else: discard update (deletion is sticky within 7-day window)
        
        snapshot_dict[user_id] = current
    
    # Convert back to DataFrame
    result_rows = list(snapshot_dict.values())
    new_snapshot = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)
    
    # Ensure correct column order and types
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot[["user_id", "email", "status", "status_ts"]]
    new_snapshot["user_id"] = new_snapshot["user_id"].astype("int64")
    new_snapshot["email"] = new_snapshot["email"].astype("object")
    new_snapshot["status"] = new_snapshot["status"].astype("object")
    new_snapshot["status_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(new_snapshot["status_ts"], utc=False).astype("datetime64[us]")
    
    # Sort for consistent output
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot.sort_values("user_id").reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
